story.iWant: to analyze 24-hour forecast data to determine maximum rain probability
story.soThat: I can make the YES/NO decision for the user
story.tasks: - Task 1: Create rain probability calculation module (AC: 1, 7) - Task 2: Implement maximum probability detection (AC: 1, 2) - Task 3: Implement intensity categorization logic (AC: 3) - Task 4: Implement precipitation amount formatting (AC: 4) - Task 5: Implement decision threshold logic (AC: 5, 6) - Task 6: Integrate and orchestrate calculation (AC: 7) - Task 7: Manual testing and verification (AC: 1-7)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given 24 hours of parsed forecast data, identify maximum rain probability across all periods AC2: Determine peak rain time (earliest occurrence if tied) AC3: Categorize intensity as "light", "moderate", or "heavy" based on rainfall thresholds AC4: Extract and format precipitation amount (convert mm to inches) AC5: Apply 50% threshold for YES/NO decision (≥50% = YES, <50% = NO) AC6: Detect close call scenarios (40-49% probability range) AC7: Return structured RainProbabilityResult object with all required fields

docs.doc: Defines calculateRainProbability() function signature, RainProbabilityResult interface with maxProbability (0-100), peakTime (Date), peakHourData (ParsedForecast), willRain (boolean), closeCall (boolean). Specifies 50% threshold for YES/NO decision. Data normalization rules: probability 0-100, rainfall mm to inches (÷25.4), intensity mapping (Light: 0.004-0.1 in/hr, Moderate: 0.1-0.3 in/hr, Heavy: >0.3 in/hr).

Specifies /lib/rain-logic.ts as business logic module for rain probability calculation. Accepts ParsedForecast[] array, returns RainProbabilityResult. Follows stateless architecture (ADR-002), separation of concerns pattern, no side effects or external dependencies.

Defines 50% probability threshold: ≥50% = YES, <50% = NO. Close call scenarios: 40-49% probability flagged for user context with "consider bringing umbrella" messaging. Core value proposition: immediate, trustworthy answers with decision clarity.

Confirms /lib/rain-logic.ts location for rain probability calculation module. TypeScript strict mode required, Next.js 16 with App Router, native Fetch API, no external dependencies for calculation logic.

constraints.constraint: Stateless pure functions only - no side effects, no API calls, no database queries (ADR-002: Stateless Architecture)
Create /will-it-rain/lib/rain-logic.ts - separate business logic from API integration and UI (separation of concerns pattern)
TypeScript strict mode required - no 'any' types, full type coverage for all functions and interfaces
Input: ParsedForecast[] array (already normalized by forecast-parser). Output: RainProbabilityResult interface
Fixed constants: 50% for YES/NO decision, 40-49% for close call detection. No dynamic adjustment.
Hourly rate calculation: divide 3-hour rainfall by 3 before applying thresholds (Light: 0.004-0.1 in/hr, Moderate: 0.1-0.3 in/hr, Heavy: >0.3 in/hr)
Manual testing only (Epic 2 standard) - no automated unit tests until Epic 5. Use TypeScript type-check and ESLint for validation.
DO NOT recreate existing functions from forecast-parser.ts (mmToInches, classifyIntensity). Reference existing ParsedForecast interface from types/weather.ts.
Follow Next.js 16 conventions: use @/ path alias for imports, export functions for API route consumption

interfaces.interface: export interface RainProbabilityResult { maxProbability: number; // 0-100 (highest probability across 24 hours) peakTime: Date; // When max probability occurs peakHourData: ParsedForecast; // Full forecast data for peak hour willRain: boolean; // true if maxProbability ≥ 50%, false otherwise closeCall: boolean; // true if 40 ≤ maxProbability < 50 }

tests.standards: Manual testing approach per Epic 2 Tech Spec: Create sample ParsedForecast[] arrays with various test scenarios, call calculateRainProbability(), verify results manually via console.log(). Automated unit tests deferred to Epic 5. TypeScript compilation required (npm run type-check). ESLint validation required (npm run lint). Integration testing via curl to /api/check-rain endpoint in Story 2.6.
tests.locations: No test files for Epic 2. Manual testing via inline test data or temporary test scripts. Future automated tests (Epic 5) will go in: will-it-rain/__tests__/ or will-it-rain/lib/__tests__/
